description:
"Yellow Monster" is a team defined by care and inclusivity. We specialize in nature-based education, aiming to help more people learn about NASA, our planet, and the vastness of the universe. We strive to transform space exploration—often perceived as a dry, difficult academic subject—into an engaging narrative that people of all ages can easily explore.

We welcome individuals with a passion for education and storytelling to join the "Yellow Monster" team.
summary: Ghost Rovers: Lost Explorers is an interactive space exploration learning platform designed to make NASA's past missions more accessible and engaging for young learners aged 6–18. We developed a Chinese and English bilingual interactive web-based educational experience featuring 28 space missions and exploration stories, organized into four levels of difficulty to accommodate different learning stages. Through age-appropriate storytelling, learners can explore the history and purpose of each mission, understand the engineering behind spacecraft and rovers, and discover the scientific knowledge gained from their journeys. The project addresses the challenge of making complex space technology and overlooked completed missions easier to understand by connecting technical information with engaging stories and Interactive and operational explanation. More than simply preserving space history, Ghost Rovers aims to inspire curiosity, encourage scientific thinking, and introduce the next generation to the possibilities of space exploration. We believe that even when a mission ends, the knowledge it leaves behind can continue to inspire future explorers.
details:
Project Content: This project, NASA Junior Engineers: Ghost Rovers - The Lost Explorers, is a bilingual interactive e-book where children role-play as NASA junior engineers, gaining in-depth understanding of seven mission scenarios and solving problems.

These missions are: Ingenuity, Opportunity, Voyager 1, the Mars Climate Orbiter, the Golden Record, the Apollo Lunar Module and Rover, and the Kepler/K2 Space Telescope.

Each mission includes the following: story, equipment introduction, challenge, scientific results, and ending, with four age-appropriate difficulty levels and a total of 28 challenges. Challenges are derived from engineering problems related to the story, such as adjusting rotor speed to make Ingenuity fly in thin air, allocating limited power during a dust storm, and identifying the unit error that destroyed the Climate Orbiter.

In addition to the interactive webpage structure, this project also includes a Chinese and English PowerPoint e-book, which can be used for teaching or general reading. The PowerPoint e-book is more stable than the webpage and can be added to, removed from, or modified according to the teacher's needs.

Benefits and Expected Impact: Children can understand the mission process through stories, experience it firsthand through role-playing, and learn through engineering decision-making by facing real-world problems. This project aims to help school-aged space enthusiasts, as well as teachers and parents, see why these machines were built, how they work, and what they teach us. It also allows students to learn by facing uncertainty through real-world problems.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used:

HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (no compilation required); three.js (including GLTFLoader and OrbitControls) is run locally as a 3D viewer.

NASA 3D resource library models and NASA image library photos, each with source credits.

Python (python-pptx) and Node.js generate the PPT (284 pages per language); hosted on Git and GitHub Pages.

AI program assistants (Claude, Anthropic) assist in writing and testing the program. Character illustrations are AI-generated and provided by the author; all are fictional characters.

Creative Aspects:

This project empowers readers to become experts on the equipment, planning the journey for these devices that perform tasks. It moves beyond the traditional model of passively absorbing knowledge. The same story caters to four age groups, with characters' coat colors changing according to the tasks. Children can choose appropriate difficulty levels and gain a deeper understanding of the equipment and its context through varying challenges.

We've transformed real-world engineering problems into interactive games, such as a detective game about faulty units and a point-and-click game to find indentations on a light curve. Furthermore, the 3D models, with their disassembly capabilities, allow children to see how the hardware works.
